input: letters is a nonempty nondecreasing sequence of one-character ASCII lowercase strings a through z, with length <= 4294967295. target is one ASCII lowercase character. Duplicates and singleton input are accepted. Integers are plain int values, excluding bool. Containers are ordinary lists rather than subclasses; strings are ordinary str values. Standard built-ins are unmodified and no concurrent mutation occurs. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Declared size bounds do not guarantee allocation capacity or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The smallest letter in letters strictly greater than target, wrapping to letters[0] if none exists. Return an immutable one-character string, not an index. Equal letters do not satisfy the strict comparison.
mutation_aliasing: All input values, ordering and caller-owned containers remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state, and separate calls share no mutable result state. The returned immutable value may be the existing element; fresh string object identity is not required. No mutable output container is allocated.
numeric: Only safe integer indices and lengths are computed. ASCII lowercase ordering agrees across the two languages, and the upper-bound comparison uses <= directly rather than target arithmetic. The end insertion point is replaced with zero before indexing.
complexity: O(log(n + 1)) time and O(1) auxiliary space for n letters. The fully included upper-bound helper uses a half-open interval and returns the first index whose value is greater than target, or n. There is no linear scan or sorting.
